blocks.title: You've completed the course
blocks.body:
Over these modules, you've explored what AI ethics is and why it matters, followed the AI lifecycle from business understanding to deployment, and seen through real case studies what can go wrong when ethical considerations are overlooked.

Responsible AI is not a destination - it's an ongoing practice. The principles and frameworks you've encountered here are tools to help you navigate the ethical dimensions of AI as the technology and its applications continue to evolve.

blocks.title: You've learned a lot!
blocks.body:
Here's a summary of what we covered:

  • Introduction: AI is a socio-technical system. Responsible AI means developing and using AI in a way that benefits society while minimising harm.
  • AI Ethics - The Foundations: Seven guiding principles - Fairness, Reliability and Safety, Transparency, Accountability, Privacy and Security, Inclusiveness, and Societal and Environmental Wellbeing - frame responsible AI.
  • Business Understanding: The decision to build an AI system must be ethically justified. An AI Impact Assessment surfaces potential harms before development begins.
  • Data Acquisition and Understanding: Bias in training data leads to bias in AI. Data provenance, consent and representation all matter.
  • Modeling: Explainability, disaggregated testing, model documentation and security testing are the tools of responsible model development.
  • Deployment and Beyond: Responsible AI requires ongoing monitoring, human oversight, governance structures and clear decommissioning practices.

blocks.title: Top tips
blocks.body: Select a card to reveal each tip.

items.frontImageAlt: A question mark, representing asking whether AI is the right solution
items.backBody: Before writing a line of code, ask whether AI is the right solution - and who could be harmed if it goes wrong. The most effective ethical intervention happens at the Business Understanding stage, not after deployment.

items.frontImageAlt: A magnifying glass over a list, representing examining your data
items.backTitle: Know where your data comes from
items.backBody: Understand your training data's provenance, consent basis and representativeness. Bias baked in at the data stage is very hard to remove later - it's far cheaper to catch it before training than after deployment.

items.frontImageAlt: A bar chart with uneven bars, representing testing across different groups
items.backTitle: Test for everyone, not just on average
items.backBody: A model that's accurate overall can still fail specific groups badly. Always test performance separately across the populations your AI will affect, not just against a single headline accuracy figure.

items.frontImageAlt: A lightbulb, representing explaining how an AI decision was reached
items.backBody: If someone is affected by an AI decision, they have a legitimate interest in understanding why. Build explainability in from the start, at both a global (how the model behaves overall) and local (why it made this decision) level.

items.frontImageAlt: An eye, representing ongoing human oversight
items.backTitle: Keep a human genuinely in the loop
items.backBody: Especially where AI acts autonomously or the stakes are high, build in real human oversight - and make sure whoever holds it has the power, time and information to actually catch and correct problems, not just rubber-stamp them.

items.frontImageAlt: Two people, representing shared accountability for AI outcomes
items.backTitle: Monitor, listen, and be ready to act
items.backBody: Deployment is not the finish line. Monitor for drift, give people an accessible way to flag concerns, and know in advance who is accountable for acting on what you find - the way Amazon, Ofqual and Twitter each eventually did, just sooner.

blocks.title: Thanks for learning with us
blocks.body:
Thank you for completing AI Ethics and Responsible AI.

This course is designed as a practical foundation - a starting point for thinking about AI ethics in your work. We encourage you to explore further, ask the questions raised here in your own projects, and be an advocate for responsible AI in your organisation.
